correctness.rationale: For odd q the eigenvalues of the linear map in the second factor, counted after triangularizing the first factor over a splitting field, are 2α, 2β and α+β twice. There are q² trace-zero singular matrices (zero and q−1 nilpotents for each image/kernel line). This gives B_q bijective maps. A nonzero traceless first factor has image span{I,X} by polarized Cayley–Hamilton and nondegeneracy of the trace pairing. A nonzero-trace rank-one factor is a nonzero multiple of a projection with kernel L and complement U. Its image condition is C(L)⊆U; the q complements, one complement, or no complements according as C kills, moves, or acts invertibly on L give exactly the kernel/eigenline term. Zero first factor contributes only at zero. For even q the image at a nonscalar X is span{I,X} perpendicular under the trace pairing because the centralizer of a cyclic 2×2 matrix is span{I,X}. Thus trace-zero C≠0 permits q³−q nonscalar X with q² lifts each; at zero all nonscalars and scalars contribute with the stated multiplicities. These are proof checks over all finite fields of the specified characteristics, not extrapolations.
